description:
Records time spent on threads, billable or not, and reports totals.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD [DESCRIPTION ...] [-m MIN] [-r RATE] [-c CUR] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] — add a time entry
  list [THREAD] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — list entries
  report [--thread T] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — totals by thread and currency; unbilled time is totalled separately
  show ID [--json] — show one entry
  edit ID [--description TEXT] [-m MIN] [-r RATE] [-c CUR] [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] — change fields of an entry
  rm ID -y — delete an entry

Flags:
  log:
    -m, --minutes N    duration in minutes. Default 60; must be positive.
    -r, --rate N       hourly rate; 0 means unbillable. Needs a currency.
    -c, --currency CUR ISO code. Defaults to the thread's currency. If neither is set, the entry is recorded as unbilled.
    -d, --date D       YYYY-MM-DD. Default today.
    -t, --time HH:MM   start time. Default now.
  list, report:
    --since D / --until D  inclusive date bounds (YYYY-MM-DD)
    --json                 JSON output
  edit:
    --description TEXT  new description
    -m N                new duration; the start time stays the same
    -r N                new rate; needs a currency
    -c CUR              new currency code
    -d D                move to this day; the duration is kept
    -t HH:MM            move to this start time; the duration is kept
  rm:
    -y, --yes  required to confirm the delete

Args:
  THREAD       thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink
  DESCRIPTION  a short invoice-style label; may be several words
  ID           8-char entry id from `hours list`

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "DORA metric validation", "-m", "180"]
  ["log", "Topics/Running", "5k run", "-m", "30", "-d", "2026-09-28"]
  ["report", "--since", "2026-09-01"]
  ["edit", "1a2b3c4d", "-m", "90"]

Notes:
  Put the positionals first. --description takes several words, so pass it last.
  Keep descriptions to short labels: search does not index hours. Record detail with `buffer add-text` instead.
  log queues a REF in the buffer, filed under the day of the work. It reaches the thread's log on the next `buffer flush`.
  rm is permanent and needs -y.
  Exit code 1 means: a non-positive duration, an empty description, or a rate without a currency.
